nodes.description: Implementation/logic address persisted at storage slot keccak256("PROXIABLE") = 0xc5f16f0fcc639fa48a6947836d9850f504798523bf8c9a3a87d5876cf622bcf7
constructor(address contractLogic) public - deploy-time initializer that writes the logic address into the PROXIABLE storage slot via inline assembly sstore
function() external payable fallback - loads the logic address and forwards all calldata through delegatecall, then returns or reverts based on success
Constructor parameter contractLogic: address of the delegatecall target written to storage
Assembly local variable contractLogic in the fallback, holding the sload result from the PROXIABLE slot
Assembly local pointer ptr (mload(0x40) free memory) used as the calldata/returndata buffer for delegatecall
Assembly local success flag returned by delegatecall, driving the switch between revert and return
Assembly local retSz holding returndatasize, used to copy and forward the delegated call result
msg.sender / arbitrary external caller of the payable fallback whose calldata is forwarded verbatim into the logic contract through delegatecall
Inline assembly sstore writing the logic address directly into the PROXIABLE slot with no validation or access control
Inline assembly delegatecall(gas, contractLogic, ptr, calldatasize, 0, 0) executing untrusted calldata in the proxy's storage/context

edges.reason: The constructor parameter contractLogic is persisted into the PROXIABLE implementation storage slot
The constructor argument is written straight into the logic storage slot by sstore without any zero/contract validation, determining the delegatecall target
The constructor executes the assembly sstore that sets the implementation address
The unsupervised sstore is what materializes the state_var holding the logic address
msg.sender supplies the calldata (via calldatacopy) that is delegatecall-ed into the logic contract, giving the caller control over executed code in the proxy context
The fallback sloads the PROXIABLE slot into the assembly local contractLogic
The delegatecall target address comes from the stored logic slot, so whoever can influence that slot controls the delegatecall destination
The free-memory pointer ptr receives the copied calldata and is passed as the delegatecall input/output buffer
The boolean result of the delegatecall is captured in the success local
The success flag switches between revert and return after the delegatecall, allowing a malicious logic contract to halt or complete execution in the proxy context
The payable fallback unconditionally performs the delegatecall for every incoming call with no reentrancy guard
The delegatecall-ed logic contract executes in the proxy's context and can call back into the proxy fallback, re-entering the delegatecall path

normalization_plan.reason: The constructor parameter only exists to seed the implementation slot inside the constructor's sstore
The assembly local is merely the sload result consumed by the unsafe delegatecall target
The free-memory pointer only serves as the input/output buffer of the unsafe delegatecall
The success flag is the direct return value of the unsafe delegatecall and has no independent meaning
The returndata size local only exists to forward the unsafe delegatecall's result data
